data.description:
## Story

As a developer, `dispatch_arbiter` correctly handles the agent's per-finding ruling array contract and a new `arbiter_processor` module routes DEFER → orphan-ticket-create and DROP → defense-store-write (idempotently, to both stores in CI), so that the cycle-end arbiter's outputs actually produce side effects in the ticket system and defense store.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] Fix `dispatch_arbiter` in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/arbiter.py` to iterate the per-finding rulings array returned by the agent (currently wraps a single ruling in a list, which assumes the wrong agent output contract). For each ruling: apply `_enforce_cove_fallback`, then `validate_cycle_end_ruling`. Return the validated list of per-finding rulings. Update existing tests + add test asserting an array of N rulings round-trips correctly.
- [ ] On arbiter LLM dispatch failure (network/auth/timeout): emit fail-closed synthetic rulings — one BLOCK ruling per unresolved critical/important finding with rationale="Arbiter dispatch failed: <error>; defaulting to BLOCK; manual review required." Documented in arbiter.py + tests verify the fail-closed path.
- [ ] New module `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/arbiter_processor.py` with `process_rulings(rulings, finding_map, cycle_num, commit_sha, pr_number=None, branch_name=None, ticket_cmd_path='.claude/scripts/dso') -> dict` returning `{"block": [...], "defer_ticket_ids": [...], "drop_defense_records": [...], "skipped_idempotent": [...]}`.
- [ ] DEFER processing: idempotent ticket creation. Dedup key is `finding_hash + (PR_NUMBER if set else BRANCH_NAME)`. Before creating a ticket, query `dso ticket list --tag=orphan:deferred_review` and parse descriptions for the dedup marker. If match found: skip create, log existing ticket ID. New ticket description includes machine-readable trailer: `Finding-Hash: <hash> Scope: <PR#N|branch-name>`. Tags: `orphan:deferred_review` + `origin:arbiter`; priority 3.
- [ ] DROP processing: dual-store write. Tracker via `review-defense-store.sh` `defense_store_write` (always). PR store via `review-github-defense-store.sh` `github_defense_store_write` (only when PR_NUMBER is non-empty). Both writes idempotent (existing behavior + content-hash dedup for tracker; PR store updates existing comment by marker). defense_type="dropped_by_arbiter".
- [ ] arbiter-rulings.json sidecar: process_rulings writes `{"schema_version": "1.0.0", "commit_sha": "...", "cycle_num": K, "rulings": [...], "summary": {"block_count": N, "defer_count": N, "drop_count": N}}` atomically to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/arbiter-rulings.json. Re-running with same commit_sha overwrites with same content (idempotent).
- [ ] Unit tests for arbiter_processor: BLOCK accumulation, DEFER idempotency (mock TICKET_CMD that returns existing match on second call), DROP dual-store with mock subprocess, PR_NUMBER-conditional PR store skip, sidecar atomic write, fail-closed behavior on dispatch error.

## Considerations

- [Bug] The dispatch_arbiter contract mismatch is a discovered P1 bug (agent emits array, Python wraps single dict). Fix shipped as part of this story rather than separate bug ticket because they're tightly coupled.
- [Dedup scope] In CI, dedup is per-PR (intentional — different PRs flagging the same line may legitimately need separate orphan tickets). Locally, dedup is per-branch.
- [Schema] arbiter-rulings.json schema_version=1.0.0; pre-commit gate (Story 14) reads this file; consumers must check schema_version and tolerate unknown fields.
- [Ordering] Depends on Story 10 (uses finding_hash from stability module).
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked.
data.title: As a developer, dispatch_arbiter handles the per-finding ruling array contract and an arbiter_processor module routes DEFER to orphan tickets and DROP to defense stores
